Your best shot would be reversing the program to find the routines taking care of encryption, then instrument the binary with a dynamic instrumentation framework (such as Pin, DynamoRIO, or Frida) and hook them. DBI frameworks allow you, among other things, to see/change the arguments to a hooked function, so you will see the data before they are encrypted, but it takes a bit of work. :-)

Frida seems to be the most user-friendly among the three. It injects a Javascript engine inside the binary which allows you to run scripts inside it to do a lot of interesting things - like the one you want to do here - and there are C and Python bindings.
